'''He Zuoxiu''' ({{zh|c=何祚庥|p=Hé Zuòxiū}}; born 1927) is a Chinese [[nuclear physicist]] and member of [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. He is a member of the [[Chinese Communist Party]] (CCP) and a self-described "steadfast believer in [[Marxism]]".<ref>{{cite news|title=何氏家族：走出寄啸山庄|url=http://news.sina.com.cn/c/sd/2009-08-17/102818451162.shtml|access-date=23 December 2013|newspaper=Xinmin Weekly (新民周刊)}}</ref> Along with [[Sima Nan]], He is known as a "crusader" against supernatural and "[[pseudoscience|unscientific thinking]],"<ref>International Religious Freedom Report, [http://www.religiousfreedom.com/PDF/nwslttr/icrfrpt040172.pdf], Vol. 3, issue 1, April 2001</ref> and became famous in China for his criticism of the spiritual movement [[Falun Gong]] and support for its nationwide ban.<ref>Craig S. Smith, "Sect Clings to the Web in the Face of Beijing's Ban; [Special Report], New York Times. (Late Edition (East Coast)). New York, N.Y.: Jul 5, 2001. pg. A.1. Quote: ''"Sitting in his apartment a few miles from Mr. Zhao's apartment, Mr. He said people like Mr. Zhao should be hunted down and locked up until they have recanted their beliefs."''</ref> He is also a critic of [[traditional Chinese medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://paper.people.com.cn/hqrw/html/2006-11/01/content_11581477.htm |title=Why does He Zuoxiu criticize TCM? |access-date=August 14, 2009 |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303173602/http://paper.people.com.cn/hqrw/html/2006-11/01/content_11581477.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Biography==
He Zuoxiu was born in Shanghai in 1927.  He was admitted to [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]] in 1945, and transferred to [[Tsinghua University]] and graduated in 1951.

After graduation, he started working at [[Publicity Department of the Chinese Communist Party|CCP Propaganda Department]]. On May 21, 1952, He published an article titled "Soviet Scientists Criticize Idealism of Quantum Mechanics" on ''[[People's Daily]]'', arguing that Mao's political criticism against Bourgeois [[idealism]] should be applied to the natural sciences as well. In 1955, he accused architect [[Liang Sicheng]] of committing the mistake of "Bourgeois idealism" and argued in favor of destroying the [[Beijing city wall]].<ref name=Guan>{{cite journal|last=Guan|first=Hong|title=Before and After the Straton Model －A Case Analysis to the Physics Studies Claimed Being Guided by Marxism Philosophy|journal=Journal of Dialectics of Nature|year=2006|volume=2|pages=97–103|url=http://www1.ihns.ac.cn/readers/060421.htm|access-date=23 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224092126/http://www1.ihns.ac.cn/readers/060421.htm|archive-date=December 24, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>  In 1956, He started working at the atomic energy division of the Science Institute of China, and in 1958, he went to the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] in the USSR. In 1960, he returned to China to join the development of China's [[hydrogen bomb]].<ref name="不是一个纯粹念书">[http://news.sina.com.cn/c/sd/2009-08-17/102818451162_2.shtml 何祚庥：我不是一个纯粹念书的人]</ref>

He was elected a member of [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1980. In 1987, He published an article claiming [[Marxist philosophy]] should guide the research and development of natural sciences.<ref name=Guan/>

In 2001 He published a paper claiming "the development of quantum mechanics proves that [[General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party|CCP general secretary]] [[Jiang Zemin]]. Jiang's theory on '[[Three Represents]]' is the fundamental criterion of evaluating scientific and technological innovation".<ref>{{cite journal|last=He|first=Zuoxiu|title=The Establishment of Quantum Mechanics and the Evaluation System of Scientific and Technological Innovation|journal=Journal of Kunming University of Science and Technology (Social Sciences)|year=2001|volume=1|issue=1|page=3|url=http://journal.chinalawinfo.com/Article_Info.asp?Id=125829|access-date=23 December 2013}}</ref>

==Criticism of pseudoscience==
In 1994, He led a group of scientists to speak out against the [[Hongcheng Magic Liquid]], a solution that purportedly turned water into fuel. He criticized officials who were taking kick-backs for advancing pseudoscience. He's criticism sparked an investigation and brought media attention to the claims, eventually exposing the Liquid as fraudulent.<ref name="science">{{cite journal | journal = [[Science (magazine)|Science]] | title = China: Scientists Seek Allies in Fight Against Pseudoscience | author = Meiyue Zhou | date = May 10, 1996 | volume = 272 | issue = 5263 | pages = 807–808 | doi = 10.1126/science.272.5263.807 | s2cid = 154272467 | url = http://www.scienceonline.org/cgi/reprint/272/5263/807.pdf }}</ref>

In the 1990s, He Zuoxiu was particularly active in his criticism of "extraordinary powers." He zoomed in especially on ''[[Qigong]]'' and related phenomena, due to the fantastic claims made by so-called masters of the practice. He publicly spoke out against renowned scientists [[Qian Xuesen]], condemning the latter's support for Qigong-related research. He advocated for a stronger role for state control in science. His crusade against pseudoscience was endorsed by four [[overseas Chinese]] Nobel Prize winners.<ref name=pal>{{cite book|last=Palmer|first=David A.|title=[[Qigong fever: body, science, and utopia in China]]|year=2007|publisher=Columbia University Press|pages=[https://archive.org/details/qigongfeverbodys0000palm/page/172 172]}} - Registration required.</ref> He conceded that he was not opposed to the practice of Qigong ''per se'' as a breathing and meditation exercise, but rather the 'scientific' claims behind Qigong's effect. He believed that Qigong claims which could not be backed up by modern scientific concepts was all pseudoscience and superstition, and therefore needed to be eliminated.<ref>Palmer, p. 125</ref>

In November 2006, He Zuoxiu gave an interview entitled "Life and Death: Traditional Chinese Medicine" in the publication ''Huanqiu Renwu'' (lit. "Global People"). In the interview He stated that the progression of history, more 'advanced' forms of thinking will always replace 'backward' forms, and asserted that TCM is 'backward'. He called the fundamental system of TCM, i.e., the belief in [[yin-yang]] and [[Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|Wu Xing]] (Five phases), totally "unscientific." He said that the increased adoption of modern medicine vis-a-vis TCM is evidence that the latter is going to be eventually 'eliminated' from practice. While he concedes the TCM has some "advanced treatment methods," he says that "on the whole it falls short of [modern] Western medicine."<ref name=hrw>{{cite news|last=He|first=Zuoxiu|title=Interview by Lu Yan: Why does He Zuoxiu criticize TCM? (in Chinese:《何祚庥为何批中医（生死中医）》)|url=http://paper.people.com.cn/hqrw/html/2006-11/01/content_11581477.htm|access-date=March 6, 2012|newspaper=Huanqiu Renwu|date=November 1, 2006|archive-date=March 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303173602/http://paper.people.com.cn/hqrw/html/2006-11/01/content_11581477.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> In May 2007, He Zuoxiu continued his criticism of TCM, asserting that actress [[Chen Xiaoxu]] died from failing to see a doctor and instead relying purely on traditional herbal medicine.<ref>http://news.sina.com.cn/c/h/2007-05-29/150613103492.shtml He Zuoxiu continues his criticism of TCM: Chen Xiaoxu was killed by TCM. (Sina) 何祚庥炮轰中医：陈晓旭就是被中医害死的 新浪网</ref> His sentiments were echoed by other Chinese scientists, including [[Zhang Gongyao]] and [[Fang Zhouzi]]. The group is now campaigning for the abolition of TCM practice.

He Zuoxiu is friends with [[Sima Nan]] and [[Fang Zhouzi]]. In 2006, He, Sima Nan, Yuan Zhong and Guo Zhengyi established "Anti-Fraud Trust", soliciting donations from the public. The express purpose of the trust was to fund Fang Zhouzi's activities.<ref>{{cite news|title=何祚庥筹备科技打假基金 主要资助方舟子|url=http://tech.sina.com.cn/d/2006-11-06/07301221159.shtml|access-date=23 December 2013|newspaper=Beijing Morning News (北京晨报)}}</ref>
